visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A middle-aged man with short dark hair and glasses wearing a black button-down shirt stands centrally against a vibrant background of lush green banana leaves. He holds a blue pen and a small remote clicker, gesturing expressively while speaking directly to the camera with high facial mobility. (2) The screen transitions to a split-view; the top half displays a large fruit bat hanging upside down from a wire mesh cage, nibbling on a string of fruits including apples and oranges, while the lower half maintains the man speaking against the same foliage background. (3) The man returns to full-screen, pointing his pen toward his temple to emphasize thoughts about the brain, his expression intense as he describes scientific experiments. Lighting is bright and even, highlighting his facial features and the texture of his shirt. (4) An aerial drone shot reveals a remote, sandy island with low-lying beige structures and clear turquoise water crashing against rocky shores. Text overlays provide source citations at the top left. (5) The man reappears, holding a tiny electronic device between his thumb and forefinger, showing the 'neural logger' hardware to the viewer. (6) Scientific data graphs appear, showing blue and purple dotted lines representing neural firing rates across multiple nights, with the man's head and shoulders visible at the bottom of the frame explaining the data. (7) Final segment features the man concluding his talk with a humorous expression, his hands wide in a shrug-like gesture as the background remains the static lush green garden setting.
visual_base.text_narrative_log: (1) [Slogan]: 訂閱挺健康 掌握健康指南. [Slogan]: 蝙蝠的方向感 不靠月亮跟磁場. [Subtitle]: 科學家可能在實驗室裡. (2) [Subtitle]: 被蝙蝠騙了幾十年. (3) [Subtitle]: 最新研究發現. (4) [Subtitle]: 蝙蝠的導航系統在「野外」的運作方式. (5) [Subtitle]: 跟我們以為的完全不一樣. (6) [Subtitle]: 在實驗室科學家早知道蝙蝠大腦有種叫. (7) [Subtitle]: 「頭向細胞」Head-direction cells 的神經元. (8) [Subtitle]: 像內建羅盤一樣告訴牠「頭正朝哪」. (9) [Subtitle]: 但問題是實驗室只是個小盒子. (10) [Subtitle]: 這些細胞是靠牆上的圖案或海報定位的. (11) [Subtitle]: 那在野外呢. (12) [Subtitle]: 難道蝙蝠靠月亮和星星嗎. (13) [Subtitle]: 但那會動啊. (14) [Subtitle]: 蛤 你說地球在動. (15) [Subtitle]: 你去跟蝙蝠說啊. (16) [Subtitle]: 要是牠的羅盤跟著月亮跑. (17) [Subtitle]: 那根本不能用. (18) [Subtitle]: 所以科學家吵翻了. (19) [Subtitle]: 主要有兩種假說. (20) [Subtitle]: 一是「馬賽克假說」(Mosaic hypothesis). (21) [Subtitle]: 就像玩早期 RPG. (22) [Subtitle]: 小地圖的北方是區域限定的. (23) [Subtitle]: 每到新地點 地圖會重置. (24) [Subtitle]: 要靠當地地標重新校正方向. (25) [Subtitle]: 另一派則是「全球羅盤假說」(Global compass hypothesis). (26) [Subtitle]: 像《薩爾達傳說》那樣. (27) [Subtitle]: 不管你飛到哪「北就是北」永遠固定. (28) [Subtitle]: 為了搞清楚真相. (29) [Subtitle]: 以色列魏茲曼科學研究院的團隊決定. (30) [Subtitle]: 直接去野外 PK. (31) [Logo]: 來源：Science/Head direction cells as a neural compass in bats navigating outdoors on a remote oceanic island. (32) [Subtitle]: 領隊 Ulanovsky 教授從 2018 年就開始找地點. (33) [Subtitle]: 條件非常刁鑽. (34) [Subtitle]: 要夠小讓蝙蝠一晚飛完. (35) [Subtitle]: 夠平讓 GPS 不被擋. (36) [Subtitle]: 還要沒人沒樹. (37) [Subtitle]: 最後找到坦尚尼亞外海的. (38) [Subtitle]: 「萊瑟姆島」Latham Island. (39) [Subtitle]: 只有七個足球場大. (40) [Subtitle]: 看過慾罷不能真人秀就知道. (41) [Subtitle]: 要放飛也要監測. (42) [Subtitle]: 他們為此開發了一個微型無線「神經記錄器」(neural logger). (43) [Subtitle]: 把誤差僅 71 公分的 GPS 跟 16 根電極組在一起. (44) [Subtitle]: 能同時追蹤位置與腦波. (45) [Subtitle]: 植入 6 隻埃及果蝠 (Rousettus aegyptiacus) 的. (46) [Subtitle]: 大腦「前下托」(presubiculum) 區. (47) [Subtitle]: 接著搭船登島. (48) [Subtitle]: 在那無人島住了三週. (49) [Subtitle]: 每晚讓一隻蝙蝠「放風」30 到 50 分鐘. (50) [Subtitle]: 同步記錄牠飛行路線. (51) [Subtitle]: 與超過 400 顆神經元的放電訊號. (52) [Subtitle]: 放風完後會被抓回來. (53) [Subtitle]: 結果揭曉「全球羅盤假說」完勝. (54) [Subtitle]: 無論蝙蝠飛到島的哪一邊. (55) [Subtitle]: 「北」永遠指同一個方向. (56) [Subtitle]: 馬賽克假說就此出局. (57) [Subtitle]: 接著他們測試「月亮效應」. (58) [Subtitle]: 記錄月升前與月升後的神經反應. (59) [Subtitle]: 結果完全沒差. (60) [Subtitle]: 就算烏雲擋住月亮星星. (61) [Subtitle]: 羅盤照樣穩穩的. (62) [Subtitle]: 好 那是靠「地磁」嗎. (63) [Subtitle]: 就像候鳥那樣. (64) [Subtitle]: 也不是. (65) [Subtitle]: 關鍵就在「學習曲線」. (66) [Subtitle]: 地球磁場是一個「恆定」的訊號. (67) [Subtitle]: 如果蝙蝠是靠磁場. (68) [Subtitle]: 那牠的腦內羅盤應該是一到島上就發功. (69) [Subtitle]: 但科學家從紀錄發現根本不是這樣. (70) [Subtitle]: 這是蝙蝠第一次來到這個島. (71) [Subtitle]: 牠們在第一、二天大腦羅盤超不穩、會亂飄. (72) [Subtitle]: 根本抓不到方向. (73) [Subtitle]: 是花了好幾個晚上穩定度才慢慢「校正回歸」. (74) [Subtitle]: 也就是說蝙蝠的 GPS 不是天生內建. (75) [Subtitle]: 而是靠後天學習地標形成的. (76) [Subtitle]: 牠們把懸崖、大石頭這些不會動的東西. (77) [Subtitle]: 記成「座標」. (78) [Subtitle]: 自己算出一一個穩定的「絕對北方」. (79) [Subtitle]: 這是史上第一次在野外哺乳動物身上. (80) [Subtitle]: 記錄到大腦的「方向羅盤」. (81) [Subtitle]: 也證明了大腦能在複雜混亂的世界裡. (82) [Subtitle]: 自己找到方向. (83) [Subtitle]: 如果你在人生的路上迷失了. (84) [Subtitle]: 記得. (85) [Subtitle]: 你腦子有問題.
